action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Untapped capability: proposed Attic (attic-widget), Gearbox (gearbox-widget), Porthole (porthole-widget)
person at the terminal: proposed Last green (green-widget), Stale ground (stale-widget), Command ETA (eta-widget)
Delight: proposed Unsent (unsent-widget), Famous Last Words (lastwords-widget), Hands (hands-widget)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Attic": The engine already puts MCP tools and the rarely used built-ins behind ToolSearch, so what is left to stow is a few percent of a cached prefix, bought with a cache miss and tools Claude no longer sees, and ToolInfo carries no schema so the per-tool cost on the card would be a guess.

stamped reject on "Gearbox": Not chosen: turn.step does let effort be rewritten, but it can only shift up from the person's own setting, nothing shows that more effort turns a failing check green, the tally cannot tell cause from coincidence, and a possible whole-conversation cache miss per shift is unmeasured.

stamped reject on "Porthole": The picture draws only in kitty-protocol terminals, so for most people it is a 40-column block-character thumbnail of a web page, paid for with a headless browser launch after every burst of edits.

stamped reject on "Stale ground": Correct and cheap, but it speaks only on the rare day an install was forgotten and is one more context line in the situation-widget family, not something a person would tell a colleague about.
stamped reject on "Command ETA": A variation on timer-widget, activity-widget and timeline-widget: the same Bash durations drawn as a forecast, useful only for the few commands that repeat verbatim.

stamped reject on "Unsent": prompt.edit cannot tell a sentence thought better of from ordinary rewording and typo fixing, so the card would be mostly noise around a rare good moment, and it is a second mirror-widget kept on keystrokes.

stamped reject on "Famous Last Words": A phrase list matched against prompts with no measurable moment at which a prediction ends, so the minutes and medians it reports are a joke counter and not a fact.

stamped reject on "Hands": In the repositories this is used in, most replaced lines are the person's own or Claude's from days ago, so the best moment is rare and the usual card says nothing worth a glance; theseus-widget already covers whose code is being rewritten.
named the widget green-widget ("Last green")

stamped pass: The only idea that states a new fact about the tree, what changed since the checks last passed, with no model call, a claim the person can verify with git diff, and nothing like it shipped or waiting.

The host reports a failing test -f (exit 1) as a plain result with no error, so the widget saw no red. Ruling: the fault is in the spec's Live recipe, not the widget; judge the widget on the second run and do not send the order back to design for it.
